planting.note: Propagate from divisions or rooted cuttings rather than seed, since mint cultivars do not come true and hybrid mints are often sterile; plant in partial shade in consistently moist, fertile soil and contain the roots to stop rampant spread.

directions: Plant divisions or rooted cuttings in consistently moist, fertile soil in partial shade to light sun, ideally in a buried pot or bottomless container to keep the running roots from overtaking the bed. Grapefruit mint is one of the citrus-scented mint cultivars, prized for its bright, tangy grapefruit-like aroma and flavor that comes through clearly in iced tea, fruit salads, and cocktails, distinct from the sharper menthol notes of peppermint or spearmint. Like other mints it grows vigorously and spreads by both surface runners and underground rhizomes, so most gardeners grow it in a container or a firmly edged bed. Water generously through hot weather to prevent wilting, harvest often to keep growth tender and bushy, and cut the whole planting back hard mid-season to renew fresh foliage for the rest of the growing season.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Herb Gardening
